name: Tuesday Night Catfight

date.source: The Scratching Post heads the card "GDWA Tuesday Night Catfight - January 18" and is itself dated 28 February 2000; the fed's own handler's page calls it "our very first house show back in January", and its own Dragon's Lair page announces the return to action in January 2000 with a cruiserweight tournament, which this card runs a round of. 18 January 2000 was a Tuesday.

appearances.note: Rekka Sakura and Marissa Monet were announced as The Grand Dragons for the opening tag match.
Joined the announce team for the four-way tag match.
Came to ringside as a guest commentator for the Grier/Lady Tiger match.
Took a chairshot from Marissa Monet in the opening match.
Counted a pinfall on a wrestler who was not the legal woman in the opening match.
Came out to threaten Marissa Monet, cut off Heidi Leick's interference, and was hit trying to break up the post-match brawl.
At ringside as a manager; took a fist in the Officer Order match and was attacked by Jen Grier after the Lady Tiger match.
Stormed the barricade as a fan in the main event, put Andrea Chandler down with a chair, and pulled back her hood to reveal herself.

matches.note: Marissa Monet pinned Black Lotus with a moonsault off the top. Rekka Sakura and Marissa Monet entered as The Grand Dragons.

A cruiserweight tournament match, fought under the fed's own twenty-count rule for the division. Yanagisawa slipped out of a dragon suplex and handstanded into a victory roll; the announced time was 14:23.
Bloody Mary rolled through after Rachael Edwards kicked Amanda Reese in the back of the head, and got the three.
Jen Grier turned heel mid-match by offering a handshake and slapping it away, then stole the win with an inside cradle out of a bodyslam.

Ruled a fifteen-minute draw at the bell, then overturned: Heidi Leick hit a powerbomb after the bell and a Fisherman's Buster onto a chair, Officer Order was stretchered out, and the referees gave her the win by disqualification. The overturned decision is what the fed's own record shows and stands as written.

Andrea Chandler pulled the referee off a two count and later hit Lanny Manson with a chair; Zaranna finished with a DDT. Chandler put both wrestlers down afterwards, and Daisy Butterfly came out of the crowd to make the save.

notes: The card survives only as a fan's workrate report, written for the fed's own site and published on it — the fed's own card script does not survive. Every match, finish and run-in recorded here is that report's.

name: Founder's Day Tradition

date.source: The card's own body (13 posts read cover to cover, msg_id qhCZCCOnT1gJ and 12 more) bills itself Monday 17 March 1997, Municipal Stadium, Cleveland, Ohio, 48,063 — a primary-source confirmation of the Lineages page's own 17 March date for the two title changes it places here, corroborating the held ledger over the pay-per-view calendar's outlier 24 February billing, exactly as the wing's own World Heavyweight reign note already treats a comparable card-vs-calendar conflict elsewhere ("Held date stands"). The calendar's 24 February date and the Western Heritage title change's own separate 21 March vs. 17 March conflict (already recorded on reign gdwa-western-heritage-r005) remain exactly as recorded — this patch narrows the SHOW's own date only, not the disputed title-change dates.

evidence.note: Dementia Praecox beat Andrea Chandler for the World Heavyweight title and Micki Duran beat Dementia Praecox for the Internet Heavyweight title, both dated 17 March 1997 at the Municipal Stadium, Cleveland.
Officer Order beat Radhi Ananda for the Western Heritage title, dated 21 March 1997 at the same card and building.
The fed's own calendar bills the inaugural card for Monday 24 February 1997 in Cleveland, Ohio, under a header reading "All dates are pending".

evidence.source: usenet-1997-DEDICATED-GDWA-2026-09-02.md (workshop record) / dedicated-GDWA corpus, this accession
evidence.note: The prematch show plus 12 further parts (13 posts total, msg_id qhCZCCOnT1gJ and 12 more, cited on the served page) read in full: billed Monday 17 March 1997, Municipal Stadium, Cleveland, Ohio, 48,063 -- confirms the World Heavyweight and Internet Heavyweight title changes dated 17 March on the held reign ledger, and the Western Heritage title change the ledger dates 21 March (the card's own body places it at this same event, per the date conflict already recorded above). Also carries the Wrestler of the Month and Lanny Manson award ceremonies, an ICW/DPW tribute segment, and a Prodigy chat-room interview with the fed head.

notes: SOURCES DISAGREE: the fed's own title ledger and its own pay-per-view calendar give three different dates for this card. Both documents are held and both are served. A same-wing editorial column run on the following Tuesday Night Catfight (1 April 1997, msg_id KnjOfLhvmroJ) recaps this card match by match with added detail: Lady Tiger beat Vonya in 18:25 with a Long Bow Frankensteiner after a plancha and a suicide dive; Wendy "Wildchild" Marshall and "Super Model" Eleanor Royal beat Nomad and her manager-turned-partner Princess Nelli when Nomad was DDT'd at 13:55; Rekka Sakura's match with Keiko Mita was interrupted by Tiffany Chandler's attack on Mita and resumed later, Rekka winning with a Fisherman's Suplex at 16:33; the Double Otanashis vs. Burning Rain tag went to a draw at the bell after Maria Urquidez's own Senton Splash was reversed into a pin attempt; Micki Duran beat Daisy Butterfly for the Internet Title shot after Zaranna's outside interference, touching off a brawl; Officer Order won the Western Heritage Title from Radhi Ananda in 38:45 with a flying headscissors, through outside interference from Andrea Chandler and Rekka Sakura; Micki Duran beat Dementia Praecox for the Internet Title with a Diamond Death Cutter at 26:44 after Madame Hecate and Andrea Chandler interfered; and Dementia Praecox beat Andrea Chandler for the World Heavyweight Title by pinfall at 53:13 after Madame Hecate threw powder in Chandler's eyes, with Zaranna revealing herself as an Organized Crime recruit by attacking Chandler post-match. workshop record: the accession digest.

matches.stipulation: singles, 15-minute time limit, Ironwoman Square Dance tournament round-robin (6 of 6)

notes: REPLACES the prior stub note ("card opening and results only; play-by-play not read in full") now that all surviving parts are read. Six results: Bloody Mary beat debuting 'Jumping' Jen Grier by submission (13:23); a Super Japan Pro Wrestling exhibition between Osamu Senshou and Erykah Draper went to intermission with the outcome lost in a missing second part; Burning Rain (Maria Urquidez, Gojira Takashima) beat the Double Otanashis (Kasumi, Kurumi) by disqualification (24:47) when the Misfits interfered, resolving all three teams' own membership_unknown gaps; debuting Crimson beat visiting Classic Championship Wrestling guest 'Sexy' Sally McClane by pinfall (13:23), flipping out of a top-rope superplex attempt; the debuting Gladiatrixes (Tawny, Rusla) lost to the returning Hyena Queens by pinfall (16:43); and Medusa Rage beat 'Brilliant' Tiffany Chandler by submission, an STF, at 9:47. On a call-in, President Denmark Vessey suspended the tag team Strike indefinitely for its role in interference at Founder's Day Tradition. A House of Styles interview segment saw Medusa Rage broker a one-on-one truce with Andrea Chandler against gang interference, with The Kingpin (not separately minted, per the Syndicate's own standing note) sparring with Micki Duran over turf. The card's own editorial recap of the earlier Founder's Day Tradition pay-per-view (already served separately) is not treated as this show's own appearances; its added match detail is noted on that show's own row instead.

name: Tease and Catfight

date.source: the fed's own return posting, headed "( GDWA ) It's BACK!.. GDWA Tease (1/2)" and "( GDWA ) Tease and Catfight ( 2/2 )", posted 30 December 1998 (msg_id Fr3f-Lg7SX0J, e7ZLH3O5EXIJ); promotions/gdwa/archive/gdwa-tease-and-catfight-1998-12-30.html

notes: The fed's own return broadcast after its second hiatus (the registry's own provenance_notes already cite this exact posting for the relaunch date and the second website; this pass serves the document and structures its own card for the first time). A new authority figure, Heather Chandler (Andrea Chandler's cousin), buys a controlling stake in the GDWA on air and fires President Rob Tucker, announcing a final PPV ("Grand Dragon Glory", billed for 14 February 1999 in Portland, Oregon) at which the American Heritage and Intercontinental championships will be merged into a new North American Heritage Championship -- neither the PPV nor the merged title has happened yet within this document, so neither is minted here; both are flagged as leads. On the card itself: a newly created GDWA Extreme Television Championship was awarded outright to Heidi Leick (no match, a front-office gift), who then beat debuting Caitlin Nevon by pinfall (a Diamond Cutter) in her first defense. A Sierra Browne/Lady Luck Cruiserweight tournament match never happened -- Lady Luck forfeited on-screen -- and Browne was instead beaten down by Shumira Kishiro and an ally, Mishakal (neither previously on this wing's own roster; Mishakal is not minted here, appearing only in this one beatdown). In the main event, a North American Heritage Championship qualifier, 'Ultima' Sarah Summers beat Lady Tiger by pinfall after Candi Bratton attacked the referee and Jennifer Grier chairshotted Lady Tiger from behind.

appearances.note: Beaten down by Shumira Kishiro and an ally after Lady Luck forfeited their scheduled Cruiserweight tournament match.
